title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Life-Saving Health and Nutrition assistance to the most vulnerable communities in Jowhar District, Middle Shabelle

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia’s humanitarian situation remains fragile following the cumulative impacts of the 2020–2023 drought, 2023–2024 floods, and anticipated La Niña-induced dry conditions in 2025, pushing communities toward a multi-season drought crisis. In Hirshabelle State, Jowhar district faces compounded vulnerabilities due to recurrent flooding from the Baarey river breach, conflict, access constraints, and the closure of critical health facilities following funding cuts. According to the March 2025 IPC update, 4.6 million people are projected to face acute food insecurity between April–June 2025, including 1.8 million acutely malnourished children, of whom 479,000 are suffering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM). In Jowhar, 193,770 rural residents (67% of those in need) are classified as IPC Phase 3+, with reduced humanitarian presence heightening risks of morbidity, mortality, and displacement.ltbrgtTUOS, with an established operational presence and strong community trust in Jowhar, proposes an integrated, lifesaving Health and Nutrition intervention aligned with the SHF Flagship Initiative’s area-based, community-first approach. The project will target severely and moderately malnourished children under five, pregnant and lactating women (PLW), and other at-risk groups, including minority and marginalized communities, older persons, and persons with disabilities. Interventions will be informed by ABC-led Community Engagement Plans (CEPs) to ensure services respond to community-prioritized needs.ltbrgtIntegrated health nutrition services will be delivered through one static (OTP) site in Timire village and four mobile integrated health and nutrition teams serving Bulo Feermo, Micituure, Kulmis Weyn, and Ali-Warabay villages. Nutrition services will follow the (IMAM) framework, combining community-based screening with facility-based treatment. Trained community health and nutrition workers will conduct routine and mass MUAC and oedema screening to enable early identification and referral. Children with SAM without complications will be treated through OTP services, while children with medical complications will be referred through established health pathways. TSFP services will support children with MAM and nutritionally vulnerable PLW.ltbrgtPreventive nutrition interventions including Vitamin A supplementation, deworming, micronutrient powders for children, and iron–folate or multiple micronutrient supplementation for PLW will be integrated across static and mobile platforms to reduce morbidity and prevent relapse. Nutrition services will be complemented by a strong (IYCF-E) component delivered through counselling, mother-to-mother support groups, and community engagement sessions.ltbrgtHealth services will be delivered alongside nutrition interventions through the same platforms and will include (ANC) (PNC) skilled delivery support, Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI), routine immunization including measles, disease surveillance, and rapid response to AWD/cholera, malaria, and measles outbreaks. Access to essential medicines will be ensured to support uninterrupted service delivery.ltbrgtProtection and inclusion will be mainstreamed through targeted outreach to minority groups, female-headed households, and persons with disabilities, ensuring safe and accessible service points, gender-balanced staffing, and functional complaint and feedback mechanisms with PSEA safeguards. Program data will be aligned with Ministry of Health systems and uploaded to DHIS2, while real-time feedback will inform adaptive management.ltbrgtThis project directly contributes to the SHF Flagship Initiative by reaching underserved IPC Phase 3+ rural populations, delivering integrated lifesaving services, strengthening community-led decision-making, and reinforcing health system linkages. TUOS proven capacity in nutrition, health service delivery, and accountability positions it to effectively reach the most vulnerable populations in Jowhar in 2026.lt/pgt
